subject: SLA addendum: monetary compensation & exit clause request
messages:
From: Alyssa Turner <alyssa@finedge.com>
To: soojin_lee <soojin_lee@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 5 Oct 2026 16:12:00 -0400
Subject: SLA concerns and compensation request

Soojin —

Thanks again for the demo last week. We ran an internal ops assessment and have a higher bar than most customers due to our regulated payment processing workloads. Two items came out of the assessment that I need to raise formally:

1) We require an uptime commitment that is financially meaningful. Credits are helpful, but our compliance team insists on a genuine financial deterrent for repeated breaches — specifically either a fee-at-risk line item (monthly fees at risk for repeated monthly SLO misses) or an explicit liquidated damages clause tied to severity/incident duration.

2) We need a narrow right to terminate (with pro-rated refunds) if Redwood fails to meet the agreed SLOs for more than two consecutive months.

I understand this is not standard, but these are gating items for our procurement. If Redwood can propose firm caps and clear trigger definitions (how latency/uplinks are measured, excluded maintenance windows, mitigation credits, etc.), we can move to commercial review quickly.

I've attached a snapshot of the dashboard metrics our SOC team pulled — you'll see the sensitivity to multi-hour degradations. Happy to hop on a call; would prefer to resolve the commercial terms before legal redlines.

Best,
Alyssa Turner
Head of Procurement
FinEdge Inc.
Attachment: SLA_dashboard_snapshot.png (image stub)
From: soojin_lee <soojin_lee@redwood.ai>
To: Alyssa Turner <alyssa@finedge.com>
Cc: marcus_lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>, lauren_bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 5 Oct 2026 18:03:00 -04:00
Subject: Re: SLA concerns and compensation request

Alyssa —

Thanks for the clear write-up and the dashboard snapshot. I hear you: you need enforceable financial remedies and a narrow exit path tied to repeated missed SLOs.

I've looped in Marcus (AE/legal liaison) and Lauren (sales lead) so we can put together a short addendum. Two quick notes/suggestions before we craft language:

- Can you confirm which SLOs you care about most (monthly uptime %, p95 tail latency for the inference endpoint, or both)? The dashboard suggests p95 latency is the higher concern.
- Is your preference that the fees-at-risk be a multiplier of monthly spend (e.g., up to 3x monthly fees after X breaches) or a fixed per-incident amount?

Plan: Marcus and I will draft an SLA addendum with explicit measurement definitions, a remediation ladder (credits -> fee at risk -> limited termination), a capped liquidated damages ladder, and maximum liability caps (Redwood standard). We'll send a redlineable PDF by EOD tomorrow. If that looks reasonable, we can book a 30-minute commercial call with your procurement and legal teams.

Appreciate the partnership here — our goal is to find a commercially sensible compromise that preserves predictability for both sides.

— Soojin
Soojin Lee
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
From: Alyssa Turner <alyssa@finedge.com>
To: soojin_lee <soojin_lee@redwood.ai>
Cc: CTO - FinEdge Inc. <cto@finedge.com>
Date: Tue, 6 Oct 2026 08:21:00 -04:00
Subject: Re: SLA concerns and compensation request

Soojin —

Thanks for the quick reply. Short answers:
- Primary SLOs: monthly uptime (goal >= 99.95%) and inference p95 (goal <= 220ms for the primary model pipeline). Both matter; uptime is the gating compliance item.
- Fee structure: FinEdge prefers a fee-at-risk model that unlocks after the second consecutive month of missing the uptime SLO. The fee would be 1.5x monthly platform fees for the first month after the trigger, 2.5x for the second consecutive month, and at that point we want an option to terminate for convenience with a 60-day notice and pro-rated refund for unused committed capacity.

If Redwood can't accommodate a fee multiplier, we'd accept a capped liquidated damages schedule (up to 3x monthly fees total per rolling 12-mo period) plus the same termination right.

Let us know what you can draft. If you can include the exact measurement window and excluded maintenance language that would speed legal's review.

Best,
Alyssa
From: marcus_lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>
To: Alyssa Turner <alyssa@finedge.com>, soojin_lee <soojin_lee@redwood.ai>
Cc: lauren_bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 6 Oct 2026 11:45:00 -04:00
Subject: Re: SLA concerns and compensation request

Alyssa —

Appreciate the clarity. Attached is a short draft addendum we propose for commercial review (redwood_draft_sla_addendum_v1.pdf). High-level summary of our proposal:

- Measurement: Monthly uptime measured on a rolling calendar month, system-wide availability for your dedicated model endpoint(s), exclusion windows limited to scheduled maintenance with 72-hour advance notice and emergency maintenance declared with post-mortem. Latency measured p95 over 1-minute sampling windows, with upstream network anomalies excluded by mutual agreement.

- Remediation ladder:
  * First qualifying month below uptime SLO: Service credit of 5% of monthly fees.
  * Second qualifying consecutive month below uptime SLO: Fee-at-risk equal to 1.5x that month's monthly fees (paid as cash compensation).
  * Third consecutive qualifying month: Fee-at-risk increases to 2.5x monthly fees and FinEdge may elect to terminate for convenience with 60 days' notice; termination triggers a pro-rated refund of pre-paid committed capacity for the remainder of the term.

- Caps: Total fee-at-risk/liquidated damages capped at 3x monthly fees per rolling 12-month period. Redwood liability otherwise remains subject to the overall contractual liability cap (2x annual fees), and exclusions for force majeure and customer-caused outages apply.

- Escalation & evidence: We will provide a time-series extract and raw incident logs for any claimed event within five business days; dispute process includes a 10-business-day review and involvement of an impartial third-party measurement provider if needed.

We tried to balance FinEdge's need for meaningful commercial remedies with Redwood's need to limit exposure and avoid open-ended unlimited damages. If this aligns directionally, we're happy to accept targeted other edits from your procurement/legal and move to a short call.

Next steps: If you confirm the draft is directionally acceptable, I'll open a DocuSign envelope and propose a 30-minute call on Thursday to walk the addendum.

— Marcus Lin
Principal Commercial Ops | Redwood Inference
